chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast) is considered Fitrah if you give it before you go out to the Eid prayer, and if you give it after you go out to the Eid prayer, it is considered Sadaqah (general charity).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between this narration and the first narration, because the way to reconcile them is that it is obligatory to discharge the Fitrah before the prayer, and it is set apart; if one gives it afterwards to the worthy recipient, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms tax given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَا تَنَافِي: No contradiction, used in reconciling narrations

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between giving Zakat al-Fitr before and after the Eid prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a critical temporal distinction for Zakat al-Fitr, noting that giving it before the Eid prayer fulfills the specific obligation, whereas giving it after is merely general charity. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (in al-Isfahani or al-Tusi's context) reconciles this with other narrations by clarifying that while the primary duty is discharged before prayer, post-prayer payment remains valid and acceptable, ensuring the poor receive their due even if delayed. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the precise timing of ritual obligations to ensure their spiritual efficacy and social utility.
